gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type by or until. Ask: a deadline for one action (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)? Twenty original sentences.

questions.explain: A deadline for one action (send) takes ‘by’: not later than Friday.

questions.before: The new bridge will be finished
questions.explain: Finished at some point before the deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
A deadline (be back) takes ‘by’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Arrive is one action before a deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Decide is one action with a deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
A payment deadline: by the 5th. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Waiting continues up to six: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Being open continues up to 9: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Staying continues up to sunset: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Working continued up to that moment: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Playing continues up to darkness: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Not … until = it didn’t happen before eleven. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Negative + until: it opens only at ten. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.after: the time we arrived, everyone had gone.
questions.explain: Fixed expression: by the time + clause. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Fixed expression: by the time. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
After ‘until’ use the present simple for the future, not ‘will’.

questions.before: Don’t open your presents until everyone
questions.explain: Present simple after ‘until’: arrives. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
‘By’ is common with the future perfect: will have finished.
Being on holiday continues up to Monday: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
‘Till’ is an informal ‘until’: dancing continued up to two.

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples with by and until.

matching.title: By or until?
matching.subtitle: Tap a sentence start, then tap the word that fits.

pairs.left: Keep walking ___ you see a church.
Reply ___ the end of the day.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. By = a deadline (one action, not later than); until = something continues up to that time.

questions.text: You must return the library books        Friday.
wrongReasons: ‘Until Friday’ would mean you keep returning them up to Friday.
‘Since’ means from a past point until now.
‘For’ is for a length of time.
questions.explain: A deadline for one action: by Friday = not later than Friday.

questions.text: I’ll wait for you here        five o’clock.
wrongReasons: ‘By five’ is a deadline, but waiting continues up to five.
‘Since’ is for a past starting point.
questions.explain: A continuous action up to a time: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: The museum is open        7 p.m. on Saturdays.
wrongReasons: ‘Open by 7’ would mean it opens before 7.
questions.explain: Being open continues up to 7: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: The repairs will be finished        the end of the month.
wrongReasons: ‘Until the end’ would mean finishing continues — but ‘finish’ is one moment.
questions.explain: Finish = one action before a deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: I didn’t go to bed        1 a.m.
wrongReasons: ‘Didn’t … by 1 a.m.’ means you weren’t in bed at 1 a.m.
questions.explain: Not … until = it only happened at that time. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: the time we got to the cinema, the film had started.
wrongReasons: ‘Until the time’ is less natural here.
questions.explain: Fixed expression: by the time + clause. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: Stay inside until the rain       .
wrongReasons: The present simple is better after ‘until’.
questions.explain: Until + present simple for the future. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: Please let me know        Wednesday if you can come.
questions.explain: A deadline for a reply: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: We lived in Lleida        I was ten.
wrongReasons: ‘Since’ is for a past point until now.
questions.explain: Living continued up to that age: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: Keep walking        you see a big church.
questions.explain: Continue an action up to a point: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: If you order now, it’ll arrive        Thursday.
wrongReasons: ‘Arrive until Thursday’ is wrong: arriving is one moment.
questions.explain: Arrive (one action) before a deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: The baby didn’t start walking        she was 18 months old.
wrongReasons: ‘Didn’t … by 18 months’ means she still wasn’t walking then.
questions.explain: Not … until = the action started only then. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: Which sentence describes a deadline?
choices: Work on your essay until Monday.
questions.explain: A deadline uses ‘by’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: Which sentence describes something that continues?
choices: I’ll be in the office until five.
I’ll be in the office by five.
wrongReasons: That means you arrive at some point before five.
questions.explain: Something that continues uses ‘until’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: ‘Till’ means the same as…
questions.explain: ‘Till’ is an informal form of ‘until’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: I promise I’ll be home        midnight.
wrongReasons: ‘Until midnight’ would mean you stay home up to midnight and then leave.
questions.explain: Arrive home (one action) not later than midnight: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: He slept        noon on Sunday.
questions.explain: Sleeping continued up to noon: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: By next year, I        my driving test.
questions.explain: ‘By’ + future time often uses the future perfect. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: The offer is valid        the end of December.
questions.explain: Valid continues up to that time: until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

questions.text: All entries must be received        30 June.
questions.explain: Official deadline: by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: A deadline: ‘by Friday’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

Arrive not later than ten: ‘by ten’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Arriving is one action: ‘by Monday’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Waiting continues: ‘until six’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Being open continues: ‘until 9 p.m.’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Staying continues: ‘until midnight’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Sleeping continues: ‘until noon’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Present simple after ‘until’: ‘until I come back’.
Present simple: ‘until everyone arrives’.
Present simple: ‘By the time you get here’.
‘Didn’t … until midnight’ = only at midnight.
Fixed expression: ‘By the time we arrived’.
It continued up to 2018 and stopped: ‘until 2018’.
Valid up to that time: ‘until the end of May’.
A deadline: ‘by tomorrow’. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Continue up to a point: ‘until you see…’.
The holiday continues: ‘until next Monday’.

Spelling: ‘until’ (one l). Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, deadline or continuous, multiple choice and spot-the-mistake. In the typing questions write by or until. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: You have to finish the test {{blank}} eleven.
items.explain: Finish is one action before a deadline, so use ‘by’.
Staying continues up to eleven and then stops: until.

items.sentText: He didn’t call me {{blank}} the next day.
items.explain: Not … until = the call came only the next day.

items.sentText: {{blank}} the time she woke up, we had left.
items.explain: The fixed expression is ‘by the time’ + clause.

items.text: ‘Return the keys {{blank}} Sunday.’ The action is…
wrongReasons: Returning is one action, not continuous.
items.explain: One action before a time → by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

items.text: ‘The road is closed {{blank}} Sunday.’ The situation…
wrongReasons: Being closed is a continuing situation, not a deadline.
items.explain: A situation that continues → until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

wrongReasons: ‘Until June’ doesn’t work with the future perfect here.
items.explain: Future perfect + deadline → by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

items.text: ‘She didn’t start talking {{blank}} she was two.’
items.explain: Not … until = it happened only then. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

items.text: Can you send me the photos {{blank}} tonight?
items.explain: A deadline → by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

wrongReasons: ‘By six’ means you arrive before six.
items.explain: Continues up to six → until. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
Until + present simple. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?

items.text: The keys must be returned {{blank}} 10 a.m.
items.explain: A deadline → by. Ask: one action before a deadline (by) or something that continues up to a time (until)?
